run.rulesInOwnWords: 1) Ingest: add that cycle's schedule row to each tier. Budgets are not enforced here. 2) Eviction: go through tiers 1 to 6 in order. If a tier holds more than its budget, move the excess to tier n+1 and set the tier to its budget. Because this runs in order, overflow can cascade outward in the same step. Excess from tier 6 is dropped (drop count). 3) Temperature check, using the counts after eviction: a COLD tier with count >= heat mark becomes HOT; a HOT tier with count <= cool mark becomes COLD; anything else keeps its state. Each tier changes at most once per cycle, and every change is logged. 4) Compaction/promotion: using the post-step-3 states and the counts at the start of this step, work out every tier's amount first (COLD: count//4, HOT: count//2). Then apply them all at once. Each tier loses its amount. A COLD tier's amount is dropped. A HOT tier's amount moves to tier n-1, except HOT tier 1, whose amount is dropped. Budgets are not enforced. 5) Reset check: if the sum of all six counts is > 38 (strictly), set every tier to count//2, drop the removed chunks, and log the cycle. A sum of exactly 38 does not fire the reset. All divisions round down. The drop count starts at 0.

run.balanceCheck: Left side: starting counts 3+6+6+2+2+1 = 20, plus ingest 17+15+17+24+18 = 91... recomputed by row: C1 20, C2 15, C3 17, C4 24, C5 18, total 94. So 20 + 94 = 114. Right side: end counts 6+10+9+7+4+2 = 38, plus drop count 76, gives 114. Both sides are 114, so the balance holds.
run.notes: A Python script did the arithmetic (scratchpad sim.py), and I then checked every cycle by hand. The two results matched. Drop components: eviction drops from tier 6 were 1 + 3 + 8 = 12; COLD compaction drops were 1 + 1 + 1 = 3; HOT tier 1 promotion drops were 3 + 5 + 5 + 2 = 15; reset drops were 21 + 25 = 46; together 76. Correction to the balance-check text above: the ingest total is 94, not 91.
